description:
Make the docs describe the repo as it IS. Stale, dead and duplicated documentation is archived or corrected — never silently deleted.

MEASURED IN THIS REPO ON 2026-09-03: **3 of 12 docs carry no `Status · Updated · Owner` banner**.

DEPENDS ON THE CODE SWEEP, DELIBERATELY. Removing dead code changes what the docs should say, so documenting first means documenting twice.

THE STANDARD IS ALREADY WRITTEN AND IS NOT THIS TASKLIST'S TO INVENT: five root files, seven directories under `docs/` (`tutorials` `guides` `reference` `explanation` `decisions` `runbooks` `archive`), `docs/README.md` links every document, every file opens with a `Status · Updated · Owner` banner, and **nothing is deleted — it is archived** with a note saying what replaced it. Spec: `rosetta/docs/reference/documentation-standard.md`.

ROADMAPS ARE OUT OF SCOPE. `ROADMAP.md` and the roadmap plans under `docs/*/roadmap/` were reconciled portfolio-wide on 2026-09-02/03 and state their own evidence standard. Do not re-mark them here.

ARCHIVE, DO NOT DELETE. The standard says so and this portfolio has paid for the alternative: five consolidated strategy documents were unrecoverable except through one paragraph of prose. An archived doc with a note saying what replaced it costs nothing and answers the question a reader will actually have.

userStories.title: Every document is reachable, banner-stamped, and in the right place
userStories.notes: 4 docs were banner-less, not 3 — docs/explanation/dead-code-inventory.md landed from 900-dead-code-paydown AFTER the tasklist measured. All four stamped with the date of their last content change (2026-08-21 / 2026-08-27 / 2026-09-03), and the tree is now 14/14 banner-stamped and 13/13 linked from docs/README.md (the map itself is the 14th). Was unreachable: dead-code-inventory, domain-addition-policy, seed-refresh-policy. DEAD LINK: exactly one, and it was the map's own citation of the standard as a relative path into `rosetta` — a private repo, so broken for every reader outside this machine; rewritten as backticked prose per the standard's own cross-repo rule. `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` reads "dead references 0 (0 distinct targets)" before and after. RIGHT PLACE: 0 directories under docs/ outside the standard's seven (only reference/ and explanation/ exist — a ceiling, not a quota), so no docs/.structure-exceptions is needed and docs/README.md says so in writing. CURRICULUM.md moved to docs/reference/curriculum.md (the standard's root is README/CLAUDE/ROADMAP/CHANGELOG/LICENSE and nothing else); its 245 notebook links repointed and all 5 citers updated in the same commit, and a difflib comparison proved the moved file IDENTICAL to the old one apart from the repointing and the banner. Fixed the two generate_docs.py defects 900 handed to this sweep: it wrote `docs/gap-analysis.md` while the tracked file was `docs/explanation/gap-analysis.md`, and it emitted no banner — regenerating now reproduces gap-analysis.md byte-identically apart from the banner date. NEW GATE scripts/check-docs-structure.mjs (index coverage + banners + closed directory set), proved to FIRE: injected an undeclared `docs/planning/x.md` -> 3 violations exit 1, a banner-less `docs/reference/y.md` -> 2 violations exit 1, clean tree -> "docs-structure: OK" exit 0. Wired into .chief/verify.sh and into CI, which carried NEITHER doc gate before. NOT DONE, stated in the guard header: the Tier-1 root-file rule, because technologies.md is still at the root pending US-3's archival. CAVEAT: chief verify runs the MAIN checkout's .chief/verify.sh, so my new step was not exercised by it — I ran the guard directly instead. GATE: chief verify -> "doc-links: 0 dead vs 0 on main", "nbgrader validate: 117 notebooks, 0 failures", "coverage HOLDS", pytest 1205 passed 1 skipped, "verify: PASS", exit 0.
acceptanceCriteria: Dead internal links are repaired or the target is archived with a pointer. A link to a document that no longer exists is worse than no link: it asserts the document is current.

Every `docs/` file carries a `Status · Updated · Owner` banner. Where a doc is stale rather than current, the banner is where that gets SAID — `Status: Superseded` with what replaced it beats a silent edit.
`docs/README.md` links every document. Unlinked is unreachable, and unreachable documentation still greps as current — which is how a reader finds it and believes it.
Directories outside the standard's seven are either justified in writing as declared exceptions or their contents are moved. Do not move a directory other files cite without repointing them.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.

userStories.title: Content that describes a tree that moved
userStories.notes: Read every doc against the tree; 10 files carried drift and all of it is corrected in the portfolio's corrections-of-record style, **[CORRECTED 2026-09-03 — what was wrong]**, so a reader learns why it drifted. COUNTS THE BATCH MOVED: `docs/reference/chief-powered-construction.md` said "221 ungated notebooks" in the present tense (chief/87 ran; the backlog is 128 and coverage 117/245, 48%, 14 of 14 domains) — the page now states no count and defers to `python3 -m praxis.coverage`, its one home; `docs/reference/gate-authority.md`'s "the 24 gated seed notebooks carry 168 graded cells" was the size of the leak when the filter landed, now dated; `docs/explanation/jupyterquiz-assessment.md` measured the library "as it ships" at 24 checksets/144 checks — RE-MEASURED rather than assumed because the DECLINE rests on the proportions, and `python3 -m praxis.gateaudit` reports 117 gates / 702 checks / 0 flagged at 354 choice + 236 short + 112 code = 50/34/16% against the 50/33/17% argued from, so the conclusion stands and the decision's own figures are left at the sizes it was taken on. CLAIMS THE CODE NO LONGER SUPPORTS: `docs/explanation/notebook-rubric.md` said progress defaults to `.praxis/` (removed when storage backends landed; `progress_dir()` is a one-line delegate to `praxis.storage`); README said "Three backends ship" and listed three while `webdav` has shipped as the fourth through `register_backend()`; README's launcher API table calls itself "the whole product over HTTP" and was missing SEVEN JD-suggestion routes and `/healthz` (checked against `launcher/app.py`'s 26 decorators, one by one); `POST /api/storage/sync` was documented as the cloud mirror's in two files though webdav registers a `_SYNC`; and `curriculum.py`'s docstring said "the 11 hand-written study domains" (measured: len(DOMAINS)==14, 180 manifest topics, 245 notebooks on disk), "Domains 1-10" (01-10 + 12-15, 06 reserved) and `notebooks/subjects/` — the last also stale in `praxis/curriculum_gen.py`, `praxis/construct.py`'s CLI example and `scaffold_notebooks.py`. DUPLICATION REDUCED TO ONE HOME: the merge gate's check list was stated in README, `docs/reference/packaging.md` AND `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s own header, all three as "three checks" — it has been six since the doc gates landed on 2026-09-03. README's "The gate" section now holds the full table and the other three point at it. NOT DRIFT, VERIFIED CURRENT AND LEFT ALONE: `docs/reference/jupyterlite.md`'s 101/144/245 (`python3 -m praxis.lite plan` prints exactly that), `docs/explanation/gating-backfill-cost.md` (117/245, 702 checks, 128 remaining — all re-measured), `docs/reference/storage.md`'s layout, the two generated docs (`python3 generate_docs.py` produced a zero-byte diff), and `docs/explanation/dead-code-inventory.md`'s named-as-removed symbols. DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE, SO IT IS REPORTED NOT FIXED: `ROADMAP.md` says "the three storage backends" and is wrong the same way README was, but the tasklist puts roadmaps out of scope. CAVEAT ON METHOD: link-resolution and structure are machine-checked; PROSE CORRECTNESS IS NOT. What I verified is every count, path, module name, command and route I could execute or grep — not that the remaining prose is true. GATE: `chief verify` -> "doc-links: 0 dead vs 0 on main", "docs-structure: OK", "nbgrader validate: 117 notebooks, 0 failures", "coverage HOLDS" (117/245, 14 of 14), 1205 passed / 1 skipped, "verify: PASS", exit 0 — identical counts to US-1's.
acceptanceCriteria: Read the docs against the tree and correct what has drifted — paths, commands, module names, counts, and any claim the code no longer supports. This is the half a link-checker cannot do and the half that actually misleads.
Anything the code sweep removed is reflected here. A doc describing deleted code is the most confidently wrong kind.

Duplicated documentation — the same fact stated in two places that can disagree — is reduced to one home with the other pointing at it. Two copies of one fact is the same defect as two implementations of one behaviour.
Corrections are DATED and say what was wrong, in the house style used by this portfolio's corrections of record. A silently fixed doc teaches nobody why it drifted.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.

userStories.title: Archived, not deleted — and the record says why
acceptanceCriteria: Superseded documents move to `docs/archive/` with a note naming what replaced them and when. Nothing is deleted outright.
Report what was left alone and why — a doc that looks stale but is the record of a decision is not stale, it is history, and this portfolio keeps those deliberately.
State honestly what this sweep did NOT verify. Documentation correctness is not machine-checkable in general, and a claim that the docs are now true is stronger than the method supports.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.
